messages:
Priya: Heads-up — sketched a lightweight integration between the SAPI (service API) and the runtime router to support automatic fallback without pushing full decision logic into every edge proxy. Want quick feedback on tradeoffs and where the state should live.

Alex: Can you paste the sketch? trying to grok where the decision state and epoch live.

Priya: TL;DR: add a small 'flight director' control-plane service that owns rollout state + rules. Proxies call a cached fast-path policy (local cache) and fall back to director only when cache miss or for re-eval. Decision tokens travel with request/response so runtime can reconcile. Example config snippet: 

```yaml
rollouts:
  my-model-v2:
    type: canary
    target: 2%
    fallback_trigger:
      latency_p99_ms: 1200
      error_rate_pct: 5
    director_policy: default
flight_director:
  enabled: true
  cache_ttl_ms: 250
```

Lee: Extra hop concern — does this add latency on steady-state traffic?

Priya: Not in the steady-state if director is co-located (sidecar or regional service). The proxy uses cached token + policy; director only in misses or during policy changes. Worst-case added tail when fetching new token or re-evaluating weights.

Sam: What about correctness during concurrent reweights? e.g., two controllers bump weights simultaneously and devices see mixed epochs. Race conditions?

Priya: We use versioned decision tokens and a monotonic epoch. Runtime rules: accept decision if token_epoch >= local_epoch, otherwise consult director. If mismatch, proxy triggers a quick reconcile call. Token example: `dec_tok:v3:epoch:234:hash:abc`. This keeps decisions idempotent and debounces flapping.

TelemetryBot: Suggested signals to wire: canary_success_rate, canary_latency_p50/p95/p99, degrade_count, rollback_count, decision_miss_rate. Alert rules?

Priya: Proposal: auto-fallback if canary_success_rate < 98% over 5m OR latency_p99 > configured threshold AND degrade_count > X. Still require an optional human kill switch. Also capture confidence window to avoid noisy flips during infra blips.

Alex: Streaming edge-case: what if fallback triggers mid-stream (we're streaming tokens back to client)? how to handle partial responses / continuity?

Priya: Good call. Runtime should implement graceful handoff: buffer a small token batch, evaluate fallback only at batch boundaries, and if fallback needed, attach `continuation_token` so fallback model can resume at the same decoded offset. That requires tokenizer compatibility or a resumable serialization contract. We'll document the contract.

Lee: Feels like this touches the session-affinity refactor we discussed — should we collapse that work with this director refactor?

Priya: I think so. Long-term goal: split router into a very fast traffic plane (pure forwarder + cache) and a control plane (director, experiments, rollouts). For rollout safety we keep simple local rules until the director is proven. Feature-flag the director so we can iterate.

Sam: I can start a POC: director + cache + token schema. Recommend starting with a 2% canary, auto-fallback on >=5xx or p99 spikes. I'll wire minimal metrics.

Priya: POC checklist: 1) flight director prototype + cache shim, 2) decision token schema & reconcile rules, 3) metrics wiring + dashboards, 4) streaming continuation contract doc, 5) smoke test harness for gradual ramp. I'll open RFC follow-up and assign tasks.

Alex: :thumbsup:
